lines.text: Every life eventually walks into a valley it did not choose.
The fields go quiet. The doors close. The prayers come back unanswered.
And in that valley, every one of us has to decide what we will say.
Three men stood in places like this, long before us.
And all three of them said the same impossible thing.
Habakkuk stood on a hillside at the end of a long day, and named every loss out loud.
Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines;
the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat;
the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls.
No denial. No pretending. Just the truth, said plainly to God.
And then, in the very next breath, the turn.
Yet I will rejoice in the Lord. I will joy in the God of my salvation.
Nothing had blossomed. Nothing had been restored.
He did not wait for the vine. He separated his joy from his harvest while the fields were still empty.
Across the ages, another man sits in the ruins of everything he built.
His children gone. His wealth gone. His body broken. Ash on his skin.
His friends offer explanations. Heaven offers none.
And from the ash heap, Job speaks the sentence that has outlived every argument made against him.
Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.
No explanation required. His trust was never waiting on a memo from heaven.
And on a rooftop in Jerusalem, long after the city has gone to sleep, a king is still awake.
Not talking to his enemies. Not talking to his advisors.
Talking to himself.
Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why art thou disquieted within me?
He doesn't wait for his soul to feel better. He doesn't ask its permission.
He gives it an order.
Hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him.
Three men. Three ruins. One radical move.
None of them waited for the circumstance to change.
None of them waited for the feeling to arrive.
Your rejoicing was never meant to be a reaction.
It was always meant to be a decision.
The will moves first. The feeling is left to catch up.
So let me ask you, wherever you are sitting right now.
What is your empty vine?
What are you still waiting to change before you will let yourself rejoice?
Your soul has been talking to you all day, telling you what's missing, telling you what's lost.
Stop listening to your soul. Start talking to it.
Preach to it, until it believes you.
Because the same prophet who stood among the empty vines finished his song like this.
The Lord God is my strength,
and he will make my feet like hinds' feet,
and he will make me to walk upon mine high places.
The vine has not blossomed yet. Rejoice anyway.
Preach to your own soul. In Jesus' name, amen.

title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: Preach to Your Own Soul
story: A six-chapter illustrated short film: a prophet among dead vines at dusk, a man on an ash heap in grey ruins, a king awake on a moonlit Jerusalem rooftop, three men on three peaks at dawn, a modern man at a rain-streaked window, and a hind on the high places at sunrise. Three ruins, one decision - rejoicing was never a reaction; the will moves first.
